originality.rationale: The closest primary result, Sangare–Ta (2026), Proposition 4.7, ALREADY proves that the left nucleus of every odd-order dihedral quandle algebra is the basis-sum line over arbitrary commutative rings. This is explicitly inherited as a special case, not a new claim. The reviewed theorem extends it simultaneously to all finite Latin Alexander quandles, determines middle and right nuclei, and identifies the universal associative quotient even for non-Latin Alexander quandles. Zhang provides the group-ring transport, and Ta the basis-sum identity. value.rationale: The associator ideal defines the universal associative quotient, a canonical invariant of a nonassociative algebra. A complete determination of all three nuclei across all finite abelian Latin Alexander quandles and all commutative coefficient rings is a substantive structural classification, not a small field table. The exact rank-one nucleus distinguishes modular nilpotence from the characteristic-invertible idempotent splitting, and the quotient theorem applies even outside the Latin case. The scope is delimited; no general downstream theorem is required. An important prior special case, Sangare–Ta Proposition 4.7, settles the left nucleus only for odd dihedral quandles; the combined theorem extends to every finite abelian Latin Alexander quandle and classifies three nuclei and all associative quotients.
